question: Will California avoid the "highest vote rule" with its 2026 billionaire's tax referendum?

calls.reasoning: Resolves No only if Prop 40 passes AND Prop 41 or 42 passes with more yes votes than 40. Markets (Oct 24) give Prop 40 passing ~23% (Kalshi 24, Polymarket 23); Polymarket 'Prop 40 defeats opposing propositions' 15%, Kalshi 'takes effect before 2027' 17%, implying the pass-but-nullified state is ~6-8%. Polls are friendlier to 40 (PPIC Sept 52-46; IGS 45-42) and show 41/42 at 51/54% (PPIC) with confused voters, so a narrow 40 win could be outpolled by 42; opposition outspends ~6:1, and initiatives typically fade late. I shade No slightly above the market-implied value, to ~10%.
calls.dossier:
- Mechanics (CalMatters, Sept 2026): if Prop 40 (one-time 5% billionaire wealth tax) gets more votes than both 41 and 42, it takes effect and voids them; if 41 or 42 passes with more yes votes, 40 does not take effect. Question resolves No only if 40 passes AND (41 or 42) passes with more yes votes than 40; else Yes (including if 40 fails).
- PPIC statewide survey (Sept 2026, likely voters): Prop 40 52 yes / 46 no; Prop 41 51% yes; Prop 42 54% yes. PPIC director: voters don't yet realize 41/42 are countermeasures.
- Berkeley IGS (Sept 2026): Prop 40 45 yes / 42 no / 13 undecided (down from 48% yes in Aug); Prop 42 43 yes / 34 no / 23 undecided; neither counter-measure has a majority.
- CBS/CNBC (Oct 2026): polls tightening on 40; opponents include Gov. Newsom and both governor candidates.
- Spending (CalMatters): Yes on 40 ~$31M (SEIU-UHW); billionaire-backed Building a Better California $187M+ ($56M vs 40, $131M for 41/42). Hoodline reports opposition spending $88.7M.
- Prediction markets (defirate snapshot Oct 24, 2026): separate contracts exist for Prop 40 passage, for 'Prop 40 defeats opposing propositions' (Polymarket), for 'tax takes effect before 2027' (Kalshi), and for 41 and 42 passage; >$5M traded across Kalshi/Polymarket on 40. (Prices withheld here; check yourself.)
- Status quo: no new tax; historically, CA initiatives facing heavy opposition spending tend to lose support late.
- Resolution instrument: certified Nov 3, 2026 California election results for Props 40, 41, 42 (yes-vote counts), not market outcomes or court rulings.
- Event window: Nov 3, 2026 general election -> certified counts; as of 2026-10-24 the vote has not occurred (early voting under way).
- Searched but not found: any October-dated independent poll of 41/42 versus 40 head-to-head; any data on overlap between Yes-40 and Yes-42 voters.
calls.reference_class: California initiatives facing heavily funded opposition with competing countermeasures (highest-vote rule cases); market-implied conditional decomposition

calls.reasoning: Resolves No only if Prop 40 passes AND Prop 41 or 42 also passes with more yes votes than 40. Markets (Kalshi 24c, Polymarket 23c; >$5M volume) put Prop 40 passage near 23%, and polls show support eroding (Citrin/Politico Oct 9-14: 46-43; IGS 52-33 in March to 45-42 in Sept), though PPIC Sept had 52%. If 40 passes, Prop 42 (polled 54% vs 40's 52% in PPIC; markets ~66% to pass) could still outpoll it, but an electorate that passes 40 is more pro-tax and the 'no on 41/42' campaign would be working, so I put the conditional at ~50%. P(No) ~ 0.25*0.5 ~ 0.13. No market matches this contract exactly; the per-measure pass markets are evidence, not an anchor.
calls.dossier:
- Resolution: resolves NO only if (1) Prop 40 (one-time up-to-5% billionaire wealth tax) gets more yes than no votes AND (2) Prop 41 and/or 42 gets more yes than no votes AND more yes votes than Prop 40. Otherwise YES; this includes Prop 40 failing outright. Resolves off certified/official California results for the Nov 3, 2026 election.
- Event window: the Nov 3, 2026 general election through the vote count; as of 2026-10-24 the election has not happened and ballots are being cast.
- Status quo: no wealth tax exists.
- PPIC Statewide Survey (Sept 2026; 1,103 likely voters, MOE 3.8): Prop 40 52% yes / 46% no; Prop 41 51% yes; Prop 42 54% yes. More than half of respondents back all three measures. (ppic.org, ksby.com)
- Berkeley IGS: Prop 40 52-33 in March 2026, 45-42 in September 2026. (aol.com/Politico)
- Citrin Center/Politico (Oct 9-14, 2026; 909 likely voters, online): Prop 40 46% yes / 43% no / 11% undecided. (calmatters commentary, aol)
- Mason-Dixon for NBC/Telemundo (fall 2026): Prop 40 yes reportedly ahead by about 10. (search snippet)
- Prop 41: nullifies state taxes enacted after Jan 1 2026 that exempt their revenue from the spending limit, and adds audits of new special taxes. Prop 42: bans new state taxes on personal property (financial assets, business interests) and certain retroactive taxes. Both are designed as poison pills against Prop 40 under the highest-vote rule.
- Spending/politics: billionaires (e.g. Sergey Brin) spending hundreds of millions against 40 and for 41/42. Gov. Newsom, mainstream Democrats and some unions oppose 40; Bernie Sanders and progressive groups support it. Press Democrat editorial (Oct 10): 'if you support the billionaire tax, vote no on 41 and 42'.
- Prediction markets exist for each measure passing; no market found that matches this vote-comparison contract.
- Reference pattern: California tax initiatives facing heavy opposition spending typically lose support in the final weeks.
- Searched but not found: head-to-head polling of 40 vs 41/42 among the same respondents beyond PPIC; any poll of Prop 41/42 in October.
calls.reference_class: California tax-increase initiatives facing heavily funded opposition and competing counter-measures (e.g. 1990s-2020s competing initiative contests), which usually lose support late

calls.reasoning: Question resolves No only if Prop 40 passes AND Prop 41 or 42 gets more yes votes than 40. Prediction markets (Kalshi/Polymarket via defirate, Oct 24) give Prop 40 ~23-30% to pass, with recent Berkeley IGS polling at 45% yes and narrowing; PPIC Sept had 40 at 52%. Countermeasures poll similarly or higher (41: 51%, 42: 54%; markets 57%/66%), and Newsom endorsed 42 on Oct 9. Conditional on 40 passing, I estimate ~50% that 41/42 outpoll it, giving P(No) ~0.12-0.13. No market directly prices this joint contract; the harness-suggested Polymarket 'local tax vote threshold' market is a different measure.
calls.dossier:
- Resolution: No only if (a) Prop 40 yes>no AND (b) Prop 41 and/or 42 yes>no AND yes votes > Prop 40's yes votes; otherwise Yes. Resolves off official Nov 3, 2026 California results.
- Event window: Nov 3, 2026 general election -> resolution 2026-11-10 per the criteria; as of 2026-10-24 the election is ~10 days away (early/mail voting underway); counting continues for weeks after election day, and close margins may be unsettled by Nov 10.
- Status quo: no wealth tax; Prop 40 failing yields Yes automatically.
- Prop 40: one-time 5% tax on ~250 CA billionaires' worldwide assets (CNBC 2026-10-22). Opposed by Gov. Newsom, both gubernatorial candidates, Sergey Brin.
- Polls on 40: UC Berkeley IGS early Aug 48% yes; IGS Sept 45% yes, yes lead shrinking from 7 to 3 points; PPIC Sept 52% yes / 46% no (CalMatters, ABC7).
- PPIC Sept: Prop 41 51% yes, Prop 42 54% yes among likely voters; PPIC's Baldassare: voters largely unaware 41/42 are countermeasures (CalMatters 2026-09).
- Prop 41: spending-limit compliance + audits; repeals taxes enacted after Jan 1 if revenues exempt from Gann limit. Prop 42: bans new state personal property taxes and retroactive taxes; Brin-funded; Newsom endorsed 42 on Oct 9 (GV Wire 2026-10-13).
- Prediction markets (Kalshi/Polymarket aggregate, defirate 2026-10-24) price each prop passing; Prop 40 is the most-traded measure. No market prices the joint 'countermeasure outpolls 40' condition. Polymarket 'CA higher local tax vote threshold' is a different measure.
- Historical note: voters often approve overlapping/conflicting measures; the countermeasure strategy relies on confused overlap voters.
- Searched for October 2026 polls of 40/41/42: none found beyond the September PPIC/IGS polls.
calls.reference_class: Conflicting California ballot measures under the highest-vote rule, conditioned on initiative passage odds

calls.reasoning: Resolves No only if Prop 40 passes AND Prop 41/42 passes with more yes votes than 40. Prop 40's market chance of passing is about 23% (Kalshi/Polymarket, >$5M traded), and polls show its support eroding (IGS 45-42, Citrin Oct 46-43), against heavy opposition spending. If 40 passes, Prop 42 (PPIC 54% vs 40's 52%, Newsom-endorsed, about 66% market chance to pass) could outpoll it, but a pro-tax electorate plus the 'no on 41/42' campaign push against that. I put the conditional at about 40%, which gives about 9-10% No. A reported Polymarket 'defeats opposing propositions' price (15%) implies about 8% No, consistent with this.
calls.reconciliation: Factual disputes: Prop 40's pass price (23% vs up to 30%). I took about 23% because three runs report it. Whether a market prices the combined outcome: Run 1 reports Polymarket 'Prop 40 defeats opposing propositions' at 15% and Kalshi 'takes effect before 2027' at 17%, while Runs 2 and 3 say no matching market exists. I could not check the contract wording (no web access). If it means '40 passes and is not outvoted by a passing countermeasure', the market implies about 8% No. The Kalshi contract also carries court-challenge risk, so its roughly 6% implied No is looser. The harness-suggested Polymarket 'local tax vote threshold' market is a different measure. Judgment dispute: the chance 41/42 outpoll 40 if 40 passes (about 50% in Runs 2/3, about 35% market-implied). Correlated electorates and the explicit 'no on 41/42' messaging argue below 50%, while 42's higher polling and Newsom's endorsement argue it is substantial. I took about 40%, giving about 10% No.

disagreements.claim: Prop 40 market chance of passing is about 23% vs up to 30%
disagreements.verdict: Took about 23%, reported consistently by all three runs

disagreements.claim: A market directly prices 'Prop 40 defeats opposing propositions' (15%)
disagreements.verdict: Reported only by Run 1; could not check wording, so used as evidence (implies about 8% No), not as an anchor

disagreements.claim: P(41/42 outpoll 40 | 40 passes) about 50% vs about 35%
disagreements.verdict: About 40%: correlated pro-tax electorate and Yes-40 campaign against 41/42, offset by 42's polling lead and Newsom's endorsement

calls.reference_class: California tax initiatives facing heavy opposition spending, combined with competing-measure contests under the highest-vote rule
